questions.question: In Andhra region, who among the following translated a few portions of Mahabharata in Telugu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nanniah**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nanniah** translated a few portions of Mahabharata in Telugu in the Andhra region.
 
• Nanniah is often considered one of the early translators and poets who contributed significantly to Telugu literature.
 
• The Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana.
 
• The translation of such epics into regional languages played a crucial role in the cultural and literary development of the regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tikkanna** and **Errana** are also renowned for their contributions to the translation of Mahabharata in Telugu, but Nanniah is noted for initiating the work.
 
• **Kamban** is known for his Tamil rendition of the Ramayana.
 
• **Pampa** was a Kannada poet known for his work "Adipurana" and "Pampa Bharata".
 
• The translation of epic texts into regional languages helped in disseminating the epic's teachings and stories to a broader audience.

questions.question: What is the approximate height (in metres) of the Qutub Minar situated in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Qutab Minar is a soaring, **73 m-high tower of victory**, **built in 1193 by Qutab-ud-din Aibak. **
 
• The tower has five distinct storeys, each marked by a projecting balcony and tapers from a 15 m diameter at the base to just 2.5 m at the top.
 
• **The first three storeys are made of red sandstone the fourth and fifth storeys are of marble and sandstone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the foot of the tower is the **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.**
 
• An inscription over its eastern gate provocatively informs that it was built with material obtained from demolishing '27 Hindu temples'. 
 
• A 7 m-high iron pillar stands in the courtyard of the mosque.

questions.question: Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho was built under which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ** Chandela**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rule over Central India**: The Chandelas were a powerful Hindu dynasty that ruled over central India from the 9th to the 13th centuries.
 
• **Golden Age of Art and Architecture:** Their reign is often considered the golden age of art and architecture in central India.
 
• **Construction of Khajuraho Temples:** The Chandelas were responsible for the construction of the magnificent Khajuraho temples, including the Kandariya Mahadeva temple.
 
• **Devotion to Shiva: **The Chandela rulers were devout followers of Shiva, and the Kandariya Mahadeva temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, is a testament to their religious fervor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solanki Dynasty: **The Solankis were another powerful Hindu dynasty that ruled Gujarat from the 10th to the 13th centuries. They are known for their patronage of arts and literature.
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty: **The Rashtrakutas were a powerful Hindu dynasty that ruled parts of the Deccan Plateau from the 8th to the 10th centuries. 
 
• **Chera Dynasty: **The Cheras were a Hindu dynasty that ruled parts of southern India from the 9th to the 12th centuries. They were known for their maritime trade and their patronage of arts and literature.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated as the birth of Lord Krishna?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Janmashtami.**__

__
 
• Janmashtami is celebrated on the **8th day of Krishna Paksha** in the month of** Bhadrapada**(Aug-Sept).
 
• **Dahi Hand**i ritual is related to Janmashtami.
 
• The main teachings of lord Krishna is in The **Gita** which is a part of The **Mahabharata**.
 
• **Rohini Nakshatra** is related to the birth of Lord Krishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Navratri is a festival celebrated over 9 days honoring the **9 forms of Goddesses Durga**.
 
• There are mainly 2 important Navratri's in a year, **Sharada Navratri(sept-oct) and Chaitra Navratri(Mar-Apr).**
 
• Diwali is known as **"Festival of Lights". **Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, Buddhists all celebrate Diwali for different reasons.
 
• Diwali is celebrated on the **New Moon of Kartika month**(Oct-Nov).
 
• **Dhanteras** is associated with Diwali.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is Onam, a harvest festival, primarily celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** is the state in India where Onam, a significant harvest festival, is primarily celebrated.
 
• Onam marks the homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali and is celebrated with great enthusiasm by the people of Kerala.
 
• The festival typically falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam, which corresponds with August-September on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Onam is known for its elaborate feasts, traditional music and dance, boat races, and floral decorations.
 
• The celebrations reflect Kerala's rich cultural heritage and bring together people from all communities in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Onam** is a ten-day festival, with each day having its own significance and set of rituals and activities.
 
• The most important day of Onam is known as **Thiruvonam**, which is the final day of the festival.
 
• During Onam, a traditional feast called **Onam Sadya** is prepared, which includes a variety of dishes served on a banana leaf.
 
• The legend of King Mahabali is central to Onam, symbolizing the golden era of prosperity and equality in Kerala.
 
• Onam is also a time for various cultural events such as **Pulikali** (tiger dance), **Vallam Kali** (boat races), and **Kaikottikali** (a traditional dance form).

questions.question: Sao Joao festival is celebrated primarily by the Catholic Christians in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sao Joao Festival:-**

 
 
• **It is a religious and cultural festival celebrated on 24 June in Goa, India.**
 
• **It is a celebration of the birth of St. John the Baptist, who is considered to be the forerunner of Jesus Christ.**
 
• The festival begins with a mass in the morning. After the mass, people gather in the streets to celebrate. There is singing, dancing, and music. People also jump into lakes and rivers to celebrate the arrival of summer.
 
• The festival is a time for people to wear traditional Goan costumes. Men wear white cotton shirts and dhotis, while women wear saris. Children also wear traditional costumes.
 
• The festival is a time for people to eat traditional Goan food. Some of the popular foods eaten at the festival include pork vindaloo, chicken xacuti, and fish curry.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam:-**

 
 
• **It is a state in northeastern India, known for its lush green landscapes, one-horned rhinoceroses, and rich cultural heritage. **
 
• The state is home to diverse ethnic groups, including the Assamese, Bodo, Bengali, and others.
 
• Assam is famous for its tea plantations, which produce some of the finest tea in the world.
 
• The state is also home to several national parks and wildlife sanctuaries, including Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Manipur:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in northeastern India, known for its natural beauty, vibrant culture, and rich history. **
 
• The state is home to the Meitei people, who have a unique language and culture.
 
• Manipur is also home to several indigenous tribes, including the Nagas, Kukis, and Mizos. The state is famous for its traditional dance and music, as well as its handicrafts.
 
• Manipur is also a popular tourist destination for its scenic beauty, including Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in India.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in northeastern India, known for its hilly terrain, tribal culture, and rich biodiversity. **
 
• The state is home to several Naga tribes, each with its own unique language and culture.
 
• Nagaland is famous for its festivals, including the Hornbill Festival, a celebration of Naga culture.
 
• The state is also a popular tourist destination for its trekking and mountaineering opportunities.

questions.question: The Carnatic classical vocalist and first ever musician to receive the Bharat Ratna award, also known as ‘Queen of songs’, is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MS Subbulakshmi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MS Subbulakshmi** was a renowned Carnatic classical vocalist and the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.
 
• She is often referred to as the **'Queen of songs'** due to her exceptional talent and contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• Her music has had a significant impact on the world of Carnatic music, earning her a place of high respect and admiration.
 
• MS Subbulakshmi's performances were not only popular in India but also internationally, making her a global icon for Indian classical music.
 
• She also received several other prestigious awards, including the Ramon Magsaysay award for public service through music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subbulakshmi** was born on September 16, 1916, in Madurai, Tamil Nadu.
 
• She was trained in Carnatic music from a very young age and gave her first public performance at the age of eleven.
 
• Her rendition of the Bhajans and classical compositions have left an indelible mark on the hearts of music lovers.
 
• She was also known for her philanthropic activities, contributing significantly to various social causes.
 
• MS Subbulakshmi passed away on December 11, 2004, but her legacy continues to inspire and influence musicians worldwide.

questions.question: Who among the following is considered the ‘Father of Carnatic Music in India’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandardas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Purandardas **is considered the **‘Father of Carnatic Music in India’.**
 
• From modern-day Karnataka, India, Srinivasa Nayaka, also called Purandara Dasa, was a composer, vocalist, and Haridasa philosopher.
 
• He adhered to Madhvacharya's Dvaita school of thought. He was a leading pioneer in the field of Carnatic music.
 
• He is known as the Pitamaha (literally, "grandsire") of Carnatic music because of his enormous contributions to the genre.
 
• He is regarded as an incarnation of Narada, so goes the mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• According to the languages of the** South Indian subcontinent**, the music system known as Carnatic music is typically connected to South India, which includes the present-day Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Telangana.
 
• It is one of two primary Indian classical music subgenres that originated with ancient Hindu writings and customs, especially the Samaveda. Hindustani music is the other subgenre; it became unique due to Persian or Islamic influences from Northern India.
 
• Carnatic music primarily emphasizes vocal music; most pieces are supposed to be sung, even when played on instruments; one should execute them in a gāyaki (singing) style.

questions.question: Who among the following belongs to Patiala Gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ali Baksh Khan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ali Baksh Khan** is associated with the Patiala Gharana.
 
• The Patiala Gharana is one of the prominent gharanas (musical lineage) in Indian classical music, particularly known for its unique style and contribution to vocal music.
 
• It was founded by Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• Patiala Gharana is known for its intricate and elaborate compositions, and for incorporating elements from various other gharanas and musical traditions.
 
• Some of the notable exponents of Patiala Gharana include Bade Ghulam Ali Khan and his descendants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Patiala Gharana** is renowned for its emphasis on the use of intricate and swift taans (rapid melodic sequences) and bol-baant (rhythmic variations).
 
• Ali Baksh Khan and Fateh Ali Khan were court musicians in the royal court of Patiala, which significantly influenced the development and propagation of this gharana.
 
• The gharana has made significant contributions to the repertoire of khayal (a form of Hindustani classical music) and thumri (a semi-classical form).
 
• Patiala Gharana's singing style is marked by the use of intricate ornamentation and improvisation, which adds a unique flavor to their performances.
 
• The gharana has also produced many renowned instrumentalists, although it is primarily known for its vocal tradition.

questions.question: Siyaram Tewari belongs to which of the following music Gharanas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Darbhanga**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siyaram Tewari** belongs to the **Darbhanga Gharana** of Indian classical music.
 
• Darbhanga Gharana is known for its distinctive style of singing Dhrupad, which is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music.
 
• The Gharana has a rich history and has contributed significantly to the preservation and propagation of Dhrupad music.
 
• Notable features of Darbhanga Gharana include its emphasis on clarity of notes, intricate rhythmic patterns, and powerful vocal delivery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhrupad** is a major genre of Indian classical vocal music, believed to have originated from the ancient Vedic chants.
 
• The tradition of Dhrupad is maintained through various Gharanas, each with its own unique style and interpretation.
 
• Darbhanga Gharana has produced many renowned musicians and has played a pivotal role in keeping the Dhrupad tradition alive.
 
• Siyaram Tewari is one of the prominent figures associated with this Gharana, known for his mastery and contribution to the art form.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the meaning of Nritta in the Kuchipudi dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Non-Narrative and Abstract Dancing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Based on the mode of performance and usage, Kuchipudi dance can be broadly classified under three main heads such as **Nritta, Nritya, and Natya**.
 
• Nritta means pure dance, **a presentation of rhythm through the graceful movement of the body**.
 
• It always reflects the** mood, Bhava, and Rasa** underlying the compositions sung for dance.
 
• **Tala and laya** are the basic concepts of nritta. “**Nrittm talalayasritam**”as given in Dasarupaka stresses the basic concepts of nritta
 
• **Footwork **is given prominence in this.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/464438ddc321ee1a17c69819c78679f4ce032f4b24035a9314be96b99c7fc400.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak **is one among the eight Indian classical dance forms which narrates stories.
 
• **Bharatnatyam **dance is known to be ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance.
 
• **Kathakali **is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatizes stories, which are mostly adapted from the Indian epics
 
• **Mohiniyattam **is a solo performance by girls with circular movements, delicate footsteps and subtle expressions
 
• **Odissi **a soft dance backed by soothing lyrics and is similar to Bharatanatyam in terms of the mudras and expressions.
 
• **Sattriya **dance tradition is governed by strictly laid down principles in respect of hastamudras, footworks, aharyas, music etc.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian musicians is known for his contribution to the field of Hindustani music for the classification of Ragas into ten Thatas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande** is renowned for his significant contribution to Hindustani classical music, particularly in the classification of Ragas into ten Thaats.
 
• Bhatkhande's work in organizing and documenting the system of Ragas was pivotal in standardizing Hindustani classical music.
 
• His classification system, known as the "Bhatkhande Thaat system," is widely used in the study and practice of Hindustani classical music.
 
• He also authored several books on music, which serve as foundational texts for students and enthusiasts of Hindustani music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar** was another prominent figure in Hindustani classical music, known for founding the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a music school.
 
• **Allauddin Khan** was a legendary musician and teacher, known for his work with the Maihar Gharana.
 
• **Abdul Karim Khan** was a founder of the Kirana Gharana and an influential figure in Hindustani classical music.
 
• The classification of Ragas into Thaats has greatly facilitated the teaching and learning of Hindustani classical music, making Bhatkhande's contributions invaluable.

questions.question: In which of the following months of the Hindu calendar is the festival of Holi celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phalguna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Holi, also known as the Festival of Colors, is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Phalguna**, which typically falls between late** February and March** in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Phalguna is the last month of the Hindu lunar calendar, and Holi is celebrated on the **Purnima **(full moon day) of Phalguna.
 
• The festival spans two days. The first evening is known as** Holika Dahan**, where bonfires are lit to symbolize the victory of good over evil, referring to the burning of the demoness Holika.
 
• The second day, known as **Rangwali Holi**, is when people gather to throw colored powders (gulal), spray water, sing, dance, and celebrate with friends and family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sravana (July-August)**

 
 
• **Raksha Bandhan**: Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters, where sisters tie a protective thread (rakhi) on their brothers' wrists.
 
• **Janmashtami**: Commemorates the birth of Lord Krishna, celebrated with fasting, prayers, and night-long vigils.
 
• **Nag Panchami**: A festival dedicated to the worship of snakes, with devotees offering milk to snake deities.
 
 
 
• **Magha (January-February)**
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti**: Marks the sun's transition into Capricorn, celebrated with kite flying and feasts.
 
• **Maha Shivaratri**: A major festival dedicated to Lord Shiva, with fasting and night-long prayers.
 
• **Vasant Panchami**: Dedicated to Goddess Saraswati, celebrating the arrival of spring and the pursuit of knowledge and art.
 
 
 
• **Asadha (June-July)**
 
 
• **Rath Yatra**: A grand procession of Lord Jagannath in Puri, involving massive chariots.
 
• **Guru Purnima**: A day to honor teachers and spiritual guides.
 
• **Ashadhi Ekadashi**: A day of fasting dedicated to Lord Vishnu, particularly celebrated in Maharashtra.

questions.question: Dalkhai is a popular folk dance of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalkhai** is a popular folk dance originating from the state of **Odisha**.
 
• This dance is predominantly performed during the **harvest season** and other festive occasions.
 
• It is mainly performed by the **Sambalpuri tribes** of Odisha.
 
• The dance is characterized by its high energy and vibrant movements, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region.
 
• Traditionally, the dance is accompanied by folk songs and music using instruments like the **dhol** and the **nishan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odisha is known for its diverse and rich cultural traditions, including various forms of dance, music, and art.
 
• Other notable folk dances from Odisha include **Ghumura**, **Ranappa**, and **Chhau**.
 
• The state celebrates numerous festivals such as **Ratha Yatra**, **Durga Puja**, and **Nuakhai**, where these traditional dances are often showcased.
 
• Odisha’s cultural heritage is deeply rooted in its history, with influences from ancient kingdoms and tribal communities.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT pair of a famous minaret and its construction year in India.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam, a classical dance of India belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam**, literally translated as the **dance of 'Mohini,' **is one of the two classical dance forms originating from Kerala, the other being Kathakali.
 
• It is rooted in the** lasya style** as delineated in the **Natya Shastra**.
 
• Characterized by delicate movements and predominantly feminine facial expressions, Mohiniyattam incorporates elements of Carnatic music, singing, and dramatic storytelling within its repertoire.
 
• Performances may feature recitations by a separate vocalist or the dancer themselves, with a strong emphasis on facial expressions and hand gestures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eight classical dance forms **are recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Ministry of Culture:

 
 
• **Bharatanatyam, from Tamil Nadu**
 
• **Kathak, from Uttar Pradesh**
 
• **Kathakali, from Kerala**
 
• **Kuchipudi, from Andhra Pradesh**
 
• **Manipuri, from Manipur**
 
• **Mohiniyattam, from Kerala**
 
• **Odissi, from Odisha**
 
• **Sattriya, from Assam**
 
 
 
• The Indian Ministry of Culture additionally includes Chhau, from Eastern India (Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal), making a total of nine recognized classical dance styles.

questions.question: M Balamuralikrishna is associated with which form of music?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Carnatic Sangeet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M Balamualikrishna**

 
 
• **He was an Indian Carnatic vocalist, musician, multi-instrumentalist, playback singer, composer, and character actor.**
 
• He was awarded the Madras Music Academy's Sangeetha Kalanidhi in 1978.
 
• Balamuralikrishna started his career at the age of six. In his lifetime, he gave over 25,000 concerts worldwide. 
 
• Balamuralikrishna has experimented with the Carnatic music system by keeping its rich tradition untouched.
 
• Balamuralikrishna has over 400 c**om**positions to his credit and is one of the very few people to have composed in all the 72** M**elakarta Ragas, He has created several ragas, with 4 notes and 3 notes and also has invented a new Tala system.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Sangeet****​**
 
 
• Carnatic** music** was written to be sung, but the voice acts as an instr**um**ent, recreating, in a way, the sound of the veena.
 
• The definition of Carnatic is a place in southeast India between the Eastern Ghats and the Coromandel Coast.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Folk Music**

 
 
• Type of **traditional and generally rural music **that originally was passed down through families and other small social groups.
 
• Typically, f**olk music, like folk literature, lives in oral tradition,** it is learned through hearing rather than reading.
 
• Traditional folk music has been defined in several ways:** as music transmitted orally, as music with unknown composers**.
 
• Music that is played on traditional instruments, music about cultural or national identity, music that changes between generations (folk process), music **associated with a people's folklore**.
 
 
 
• ​**Haveli Sangeet****​**
 
 
• It is a pure form of classical music consisting of numerous alaaps, gaans and pads** sung in the temples**.
 
• Haveli Sangeet and Shastriya Sangeet are similar to each other and the age-old sangeet is dedicated in praise of the almighty. 
 
• **Haveli Sangeet is a form of Hindustani classical music sung in havelis.**
 
• The essential component is **dhrupad.**
 
• It originated in **Mathura in Braj, northern India.**
 
• It takes the form of devotional songs sung daily to Krishna by the **Pushtimarg sect**.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Sangeet****​**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is the classical music of the Indian subcontinent's northern regions.
 
• It's also known as Shastriya** sangeet** or North Indian classical music.
 
• Its roots can be traced back to the 12th century CE when it split from Carnatic music, the Southern classical tradition.
 
• Dhrupad, Khyal, and Tarana are the three major vocal genres or styles associated with Hindustani classical music.
 
• Dhamar, Trivat, Chaiti, Kajari, Tappa, Tap-Khyal, Ashtapadis, Thumri, Dadra, Ghazal, and Bhajan are light classical genres that do not follow the strict principles of classical music.
 
• Tansen is widely regarded as the founder of Hindustani music.
 
• Alapana__:
 
 
• The exposition of a raga or tone is known as alapana or ragam.
 
• It is the first element of Ragam Tanam Pallavi (RTP), which demonstrates a Carnatic musician's ability to comprehend a raga and compose music to accompany it.

questions.question: Thullal dance originated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thullal, **a solo satiric dance form, **originated in Kerala, **India, during the **18th century,** credited to **Kunchan Nambiar,** one of the renowned **Malayalam poets **known as the **Prachina Kavithrayam**.
 
• This art form combines dance and drama, with the performer singing and narrating stories, which requires considerable skill.
 
• Thullal often portrays aspects of the literary, artistic, and cultural milieu of **medieval Kerala**, with episodes from Indian epics presented through straightforward Malayalam poetry.
 
• There are three primary forms of thullal: Ottan Thullal, Parayan Thullal, and Sheethankan Thullal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some **traditional dance forms **from **Kerala**:
 
• **Kathakali: **Known for its elaborate makeup and expressive movements, Kathakali is a classical dance-drama that depicts stories from Hindu mythology through captivating performances.
 
• **Mohiniyattam:** Celebrated for its graceful movements and subtle expressions, Mohiniyattam is a traditional dance form performed mainly by women, showcasing stories of love and devotion.
 
• **Thullal: **Originating in the 18th century, Thullal is a solo satirical dance form introduced by Kunchan Nambiar, featuring storytelling through song and dance, often reflecting Kerala's literary and cultural life.
 
• **Koodiyattam: **Recognized as one of the oldest classical theater forms in the world, Koodiyattam combines dance, music, and drama to present stories from Hindu epics with intricate choreography and vibrant costumes.

questions.question: According to Hindu calendar, Diwali falls in which of the following months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartika**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, **Diwali** falls in the month of **Kartika**.
 
• Diwali, also known as the **Festival of Lights**, is one of the most important festivals in Hindu culture.
 
• The festival signifies the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm and involves lighting oil lamps, bursting fireworks, and sharing sweets with friends and family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Diwali is celebrated over five days, with each day having its own significance and rituals.
 
• The festival usually falls between mid-October and mid-November, depending on the lunar calendar.
 
• It is also a time for cleaning and decorating homes, buying new clothes, and performing religious rituals.
 
• In addition to Hindus, Diwali is also celebrated by Sikhs, Jains, and some Buddhists.

questions.question: Mahavir Jayanti is a major festival of the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahavir Jayanti is celebrated by the Jain community commemorating the birth of Lord Mahavira, the founder of Jainism. 
 
• Mahavira is the 24th and the last Tirthankara, who preached the essence of life, virtue, and non-violence towards all living beings.
 
• According to the Swetambaras, he was born in 599 BC but the Digambar school of Jainism believes that Mahavira was born in 615 BC. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Lord Mahavir, also referred to as Indian sage Vardhamana, was born in Kundalagrama, Bihar, as a son to king Siddartha and Queen Trishala. 
 
• At the age of 30, he renounced his throne and other worldly possessions and spent twelve years of his life as an ascetic.
 
• At the age of 72, he attained nirvana and devoted the rest of his life to preach spiritual freedom.
